text_blocks.snippet: Balanitis, the inflammation of the glans penis (head of the penis), often appears as redness, swelling, and sometimes a rash or discharge on the glans and/or foreskin. In uncircumcised men, it can also affect the foreskin. Symptoms can include pain, itching, and difficulty retracting the foreskin.
snippet_highlighted_words: redness, swelling, and sometimes a rash or discharge on the glans and/or foreskin

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at what balanitis can look like:

list.snippet: Redness and swelling: The most common signs are redness and swelling of the glans and/or foreskin.
Rash or lesions: The affected area may develop a rash, small bumps (papules), or sores.
Discharge: A foul-smelling discharge under the foreskin may be present.
Pain or itching: Discomfort or itching in the affected area is common.
Difficulty retracting the foreskin: In uncircumcised individuals, balanitis can make it difficult or painful to retract the foreskin.

text_blocks.snippet: Balanitis can be caused by various factors, including infections (bacterial or fungal), skin conditions, irritation, or allergic reactions. In some cases, balanitis can be a sign of other conditions like diabetes or sexually transmitted infections. If you experience any of these symptoms, it's important to see a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment, according to Healthline and Medical News Today.

text_blocks.snippet: A rash on the foreskin can be caused by various factors, including infections, skin conditions, or irritations. It's essential to identify the cause to determine the appropriate treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: can be caused by various factors, including infections, skin conditions, or irritations

list.snippet: Fungal Infections (Thrush): Often caused by Candida albicans, leading to redness, itching, and a white, cheesy discharge.
Bacterial Infections: Can result in redness, swelling, and pus-filled bumps.
STIs: Certain sexually transmitted infections, like herpes or syphilis, can cause sores or rashes.
Psoriasis: Can cause red, scaly, and itchy patches.
Eczema: May lead to dry, itchy, and inflamed skin.
Lichen Sclerosus: Can cause white, thickened patches, often with itching.
Contact Dermatitis: A reaction to irritants like soap, detergents, or fragrances.
Poor Hygiene: Buildup of smegma (a natural secretion) can irritate the skin and cause inflammation.
Irritation from Soaps or Lotions: Certain soaps, lotions, or even condoms can cause irritation and rashes.
Jock Itch: A fungal infection that can cause a red, itchy, and scaly rash in the groin area.
Drug Reactions: Certain medications can cause rashes as a side effect.
If the rash is painful, persistent, or accompanied by other symptoms like fever or discharge, it's important to see a doctor.
If you suspect an STI, it's crucial to get tested and treated promptly.
If over-the-counter treatments don't improve the rash, consult a healthcare professional.
Practice good hygiene by washing the genital area with mild soap and water, and drying it thoroughly.
Avoid using harsh soaps, lotions, or scented products in the genital area.
If you have a known skin condition, follow your doctor's recommendations for treatment and management.
